rationale: The decided-regression witness came from a delayed Prepare. This successor tests the same path from an ordinary fault: a single lost Prepare leaves node 5 following the cut leader, and the documented reconnected(pid) call sends a PrepareReq to the new leader, whose Accept-phase Promise reply is answered with an AcceptSync carrying the lower decided index. The aim is to show whether one dropped message plus the library's own reconnect mechanism suffices, without any artificial delivery ordering beyond the loss.

scope.description: Five-node in-process scenario where the new leader's Prepare addressed to node 5 is lost outright. Node 5 keeps following the cut leader, the probe calls the public reconnected(2) to report the restored connection, and node 5 promises to the new leader while that leader is already in Accept.
assumptions: One Prepare message is lost; the rest of the exchange between nodes 2, 3 and 4 is delivered normally.
The OpenPaxos reconnected(pid) call is used exactly as the public API documents for a re-established connection.
Accepted replies from nodes 3 and 4 are held to keep the new leader below decided 5 while node 5 reconnects.
No ticks are called, so leadership is obtained only through try_become_leader.
excluded: Snapshots, flexible quorums, batching, reconfiguration, BLE elections and multiple lost messages.

experiment.prefix: Decide Value(1..=4) on all five nodes; append Value(5) and deliver its AcceptDecide to 2,3,5 (purged for 4), deliver the Accepteds to node 1, deliver the Decide only to node 5; emit ready with node 5 decided 5 and node 2 decided 4. Cut node 1; elect node 2; extract and discard the Prepare addressed to node 5; deliver the Prepare to 3 and 4; collect and deliver their promises so node 2 enters Accept; deliver its AcceptSyncs to 3 and 4; extract and hold their Accepted replies. Call node5.reconnected(2), collect and record a PrepareReq to node 2, deliver it, collect and record the resulting Prepare to node 5, deliver it, collect and record node 5's Promise, deliver it, collect and record the AcceptSync to node 5, deliver it, collect and record node 5's Accepted reply. Emit late_sync phase=after_sync with decided, decided_before, entry_status, decided_leader2, regressed, n5_accept, n2_accept, lost_prepare_count and the four message flags. Then deliver the held Accepted replies, settle among nodes 2..5, and emit after_redecide.

comparisons.description: After node 5 reconnects and applies the AcceptSync from the lower-decided leader, its decided index drops and the entry at index 4 reads undecided.
